channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway Construction Advances with Tunnel and Bridge Work
item.description: Construction on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is progressing, with significant work completed on tunnels and bridges in Kyrgyzstan. Kyrgyz Railways reports that approximately 22% of the total construction is expected to be finished by the end of 2026. The project aims for a 2031 operational launch, potentially earlier.

item.title: Afghan-Pakistan Conflict Hinders Central-South Asian Trade, Kazakhstan Revises Targets
item.description: The ongoing conflict between Afghanistan and Pakistan is significantly hindering trade between Central and South Asia. Kazakhstan has revised its annual bilateral trade turnover target with Pakistan downwards to approximately $645 million, a decrease from earlier optimistic projections. Uzbekistan also faces challenges in meeting its trade goals.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Professional Training for Labor Migrants
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its state policy in employment by focusing on professional training for labor migrants. The goal is to prepare citizens not just as a workforce, but as professionals with modern skills and foreign language proficiency. This initiative aims to expand opportunities for young people seeking employment abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Mining Industry Reviews Performance and Sets Future Goals
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology held a meeting to analyze the sector's performance from January to September. Key priorities include modernizing processes, expanding geological exploration, optimizing resource use, and enhancing enterprise efficiency. The ministry aims to strengthen control over digitalization and ensure the implementation of set tasks.

item.title: Asian Cup Football Tournament Postponed to Late 2027 Due to Regional Instability
item.description: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup, originally scheduled for January 2027, to December 2027-January 2028. The decision cites "exceptional circumstances" and "logistical complexities" arising from Middle East conflict. This impacts preparations for qualified teams including Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Modernizes Bukhara Oil Refinery to Boost High-Quality Fuel Production
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Bukhara Oil Refinery to review a modernization project aimed at increasing crude processing capacity by 2.5 million tons annually. The $328 million project will enhance production of Euro-5 compliant gasoline (AI-92 and AI-95) by installing hydrotreating and naphtha isomerization units.

item.title: SCO Plus Security Dialogue on Digital Transformation to Convene in Samarkand
item.description: The first SCO Plus expert dialogue on security, focusing on countering terrorism and extremism in the digital age, will be held in Samarkand from November 5-6, 2026. The initiative, proposed by Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, will be chaired by the head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service. The event will gather representatives from SCO member states, observers, dialogue partners, and international organizations to discuss the impact of new technologies on security challenges.

item.title: Uzbekistan's WTO Accession: Progress and Future Tasks Discussed in Tashkent
item.description: A press conference in Tashkent reviewed Uzbekistan's progress in joining the World Trade Organization. Discussions covered economic reforms, results of negotiation rounds, and upcoming priorities. Over 400 questions from member states were addressed, and significant progress was made in bilateral negotiations on market access for goods and services. WTO accession aims to expand foreign trade and improve the investment climate.

item.title: Kazakhstan Women's National Team Learns UEFA Nations League Opponents
item.description: The draw for the UEFA Women's Nations League 2027 group stage was held in Nyon, Switzerland. The Kazakhstan team was placed in Group 6 of League C, where they will face Montenegro and Armenia. The first two rounds of the tournament are scheduled for late February and early March next year.

item.title: Turkmenistan Security Council Reviews Ten-Month Performance, Discusses Security Enhancements
item.description: Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow chaired a Security Council meeting reviewing the performance of military and law enforcement agencies over the past ten months. Discussions focused on ensuring national security and stability, strengthening the material and technical base of these agencies, and further improving their operations. The meeting also covered the progress of the conscription season and professional development of military personnel.

item.title: Tensions Surrounding Iran Drive Up Oil Prices, Brent Crude Reaches $105 Per Barrel
item.description: Tensions surrounding Iran, following a strike by the US on Qeshm Island, have caused oil prices to rise. Brent crude reached $105 per barrel, and WTI traded at $97. Experts suggest oil prices may continue to increase due to the prolonged conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China Discuss Joint Projects for Poverty Reduction Using Chinese Experience
item.description: Officials from Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region met with a Chinese delegation to discuss poverty reduction projects. They explored implementing joint initiatives based on China's experience, focusing on agricultural processing and export. China expressed interest in sharing expertise and investing in the region.

item.title: Europe Airports on Alert Following Multiple Bomb Threats
item.description: Airports in Poland, Spain, and Bulgaria temporarily closed or conducted security checks after receiving reports of potential explosive devices on at least seven passenger planes. A LOT Polish Airlines flight from London to Warsaw made an emergency landing in Warsaw-Modlin. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakh Seafarer Among Crew Released from India-Arrested Tanker
item.description: A second group of seven sailors, including a citizen of Kazakhstan, has been removed from the tanker Unity, arrested in India. The Kazakh Foreign Ministry confirmed preparations for his return. The first group of seven sailors has already returned home. Nine crew members remain awaiting a replacement team.

item.title: Linguistic Discrimination in Badakhshan: Pashto Imposed Over Local Persian and Uzbek Languages
item.description: The imposition of Pashto in public messages and banners in Badakhshan raises concerns about linguistic justice and equality. While respecting all languages, the article argues that neglecting the dominant Persian and spoken Uzbek languages in favor of Pashto disregards the identity and dignity of local residents. The author questions why public communications are not in languages understood by the local population.

item.title: Kazakhstan Labor Ministry Clarifies Rules on Probationary Employee Salaries
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has clarified that employee salaries during the probation period must be paid in full and on time, as stipulated in the labor contract. The probation period generally does not exceed three months, but can be extended to six months for certain senior positions. Employees retain all basic labor rights and guarantees during this period.

item.title: Kazakhstan Weather Alert: Heavy Rains, Frost, and Flood Risks Issued for November 4
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kazhydromet has issued storm warnings for 17 regions on November 4, anticipating heavy rains in the mountains of Turkestan, frost up to -7 degrees Celsius in Zhetisu, and snow/ice in the east. Flood risks are also highlighted due to potential river level rises.

item.title: Ukraine President Zelensky Reports 33 Killed in Russian Attack on Southeastern School
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that 33 people were killed and 50 remain trapped under rubble following a Russian attack on a school in the southeastern village of Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast. The school was reportedly used as a distribution center and shelter.

item.title: Astana to Host Key World Anti-Doping Agency Meetings in 2026
item.description: Astana will become a center for the global fight against doping, hosting significant meetings of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) in November 2026. The Executive Committee and Foundation Board sessions will gather anti-doping leaders to discuss system development, clean sport principles, and international cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tungsten Developer Cove Kaz Plans U.S. Listing After Dropping Merger
item.description: Cove Kaz, developing tungsten deposits in Kazakhstan, has abandoned its merger with Skyline Builders and now plans a direct U.S. stock exchange listing in early 2027. A $32 million investment commitment will fund project development, aiming to shorten the time to production.

item.title: Zelensky Confirms Ukrainian Hackers Breached Russian Emergency Ministry Alert System
item.description: Ukrainian hackers have successfully breached Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations alert system, President Zelensky confirmed. This follows an earlier incident where a Ukrainian air raid alert app was compromised, sending false nuclear threat messages. The breach of the Russian system occurred shortly after the Ukrainian app incident.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Enhance Protection Measures for Citizens Working Abroad
item.description: Kazakhstan will strengthen protection measures for its citizens working abroad as part of a national plan against human trafficking for 2027-2029. The plan prioritizes preventing forced labor and protecting migrant workers' rights. Information on recruitment agencies and measures against exploitation will be published.

item.title: Iran Hosts Quadrilateral Talks on Afghanistan
item.description: Iran has hosted quadrilateral talks concerning Afghanistan. The discussions focused on issues related to the country. Further details on the specific outcomes or participants were not immediately available from the provided text.

item.title: 12-Year-Old Girl Reports Childhood Sexual Abuse After Seeking Help from ChatGPT
item.description: A 12-year-old girl in Pavlodar sought help from ChatGPT after being sexually abused as a child. The AI advised her to contact a psychologist and provided emergency service numbers. This led to the investigation and prosecution of her 39-year-old maternal uncle, who was sentenced to 20 years in prison for the crime, which occurred in 2020.

item.title: Taliban Ban Needy Women in Helmand from Working and Begging
item.description: Needy women in Helmand, who are heads of households, report being banned by the Taliban from both working and begging. These women express concern over their children going hungry and their inability to meet basic needs. The Taliban have reportedly established a committee to prevent begging and have imposed restrictions on women's economic activities.

item.title: UN: Hunger and Malnutrition on the Rise in Southern Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports increasing hunger and malnutrition in southern Afghanistan. Parents are skipping meals to feed their children, and declining financial resources limit families' access to necessary assistance. OCHA emphasizes the need for both immediate food aid and livelihood opportunities for vulnerable families.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Requests Annual Quota for Aquatic Biological Resources from Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has requested an annual quota from Russia for the extraction of aquatic biological resources. The Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry, Erlist Akunbekov, discussed this and other cooperation areas with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Patrushev. Kyrgyzstan also proposed joint projects for fishing and aquaculture development.

item.title: Russian Bailiffs Gain Access to CIS Citizens' Bank Accounts and Assets
item.description: Russian bailiffs will be able to access information on bank accounts, income, and property of Russian citizens in CIS countries. President Putin ratified an agreement allowing Russia's Federal Bailiff Service to request data from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Belarus, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan.

item.title: Almaty Designates Test Sites and Routes for Autonomous Vehicles
item.description: Almaty has identified a testing polygon in the Almaly district and public road routes for autonomous vehicles. A total of 122 roads, including the Eastern Bypass and Kuldzhinsky Trakt, are designated for vehicles with conditional and high automation, according to the city's akimat.

item.title: Atyrau Police Distribute Reflective Collars to Prevent Livestock-Related Accidents
item.description: The Atyrau region police department has distributed approximately 1,000 reflective collars to livestock owners along the Dosser-Kulsary highway. These collars, worn on animal necks, will help drivers spot livestock at night, aiming to reduce road accidents and ensure driver safety.

item.title: Foreign Expert Analyzes Kazakhstan's President Tokayev's Address and Constitutional Reforms
item.description: Dr. Ahmed Mustafa, President of the Center for Asian Studies and Translation (Egypt), has provided an analytical review of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address and recent constitutional reforms in Kazakhstan. He highlighted that Kazakhstan has strengthened its sovereignty and become a leading state in Central Asia, serving as a strategic bridge between Asia and Europe.

item.title: UN Envoy Warns of Declining General Education Amidst Madrasa Expansion in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Permanent Representative, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, expressed concern over the decline of general education and the expansion of religious madrasas, warning it challenges the future of Afghan youth. He noted over 23,000 religious institutions were registered or converted by the Taliban. Faiq stressed the need for scientific and digital skills for youth in a changing world.

item.title: 2027 AFC Asian Cup Postponed to Late 2027
item.description: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has officially announced the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, originally scheduled for January-February 2027 in Saudi Arabia. The tournament will now take place from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028. The AFC cited complex regional circumstances, including logistical and transport disruptions, as reasons for the delay.

item.title: Almaty Police Discover Drugs Hidden Inside Cookies
item.description: Almaty police seized approximately 150 grams of plant-based drugs concealed within cookies. A local resident was detained on suspicion of illegal drug trafficking. During a search, officers found the drugs, along with electronic scales, zip-lock bags, tape, and plasticine.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan president threatens to retake gas system from Gazprom
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov stated he may reclaim the country's gas system from Russia's Gazprom if the company fails to fulfill its gasification obligations. Japarov mentioned the system was sold to Gazprom in 2013 for one dollar and that the agreement includes gasification commitments.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Zarbdar district governor dismissed after kindergarten head's murder
item.description: The governor of Zarbdar district in Uzbekistan, Bekzod Toshpulatov, was dismissed from his post on October 31, following the murder of the local kindergarten head. His deputy, Alisher Erjigitov, has temporarily assumed the duties of district governor.

item.title: Russia Doubles List of Offenses for Migrant Deportation
item.description: As of November 3, Russia has doubled the list of violations for which foreign citizens can be deported, increasing grounds from 22 to 45. New rules now include offenses like petty hooliganism, participation in unauthorized rallies, and spreading discrediting information about the Russian Armed Forces.

item.title: Eight Kazakh Citizens Remain Hospitalized in Tashkent Following Poisoning Incident
item.description: Eight Kazakh citizens, including six young footballers, are still hospitalized in Tashkent after suffering poisoning during sports competitions. A total of 18 people were hospitalized, with 10 discharged after treatment. The remaining eight, including two adults and six children, are in stable condition and receiving medical care.

item.title: Key Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan Member Killed in Pakistani Airstrike in Kandahar
item.description: Mullah Aminullah, a key member of Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), was reportedly killed in a Pakistani airstrike in Kandahar city's Firqah area on September 24. Sources indicate Aminullah was targeted after a meeting with Taliban leaders, while unaccompanied by bodyguards.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Stresses Need for Women and Youth Participation in Future Decisions
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Permanent Representative, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, emphasized that women and youth must have a significant role in decisions shaping their future. He stated the mission is committed to conveying their voices to the UN, noting past years have seen instability and restrictions for Afghan youth.
